preamble: Book 8 is the capstone of the AI Edition. Its invariants are not new axioms appended to the series — they are the meta-theoretical ground conditions that the entire series has been presupposing. The Nature of Structure (NoS) turns the AI Edition's own tools — FFT primitives, OR opacity analysis, TEL formal encoding, SARG structural argumentation — on the question of what structure itself is. These four invariants constitute the structural realist commitment that licenses the entire framework.

invariants.label: Structural Autonomy
invariants.statement: Structure is not reducible to the intrinsic properties of its constituent nodes. The structural properties of a system are irreducible to — and not fully determined by — the intrinsic, non-relational properties of the elements that participate in it. Structure exists at the level of relations, not at the level of relata.
invariants.corollary: Removing the relational configuration from S and retaining only the intrinsic node properties does not yield S. Any model that reconstructs structure from node-intrinsic properties alone is not a structural model — it is a node-intrinsic model that borrows structural vocabulary.
invariants.violation: Defining a structure's identity, behavior, or constraint satisfaction entirely in terms of the intrinsic properties of its nodes; treating structural properties as supervening on node-intrinsic properties without residue; asserting that swapping nodes with identical intrinsic properties produces the same structure regardless of relational configuration.
cross_references: INV-001 (Book 1 Structural Identity — autonomy is the metaphysical ground of structural identity)
INV-NOS-002 (Relational Primacy — the relata are constituted by their relations, not prior to them)
invariants.meta_note: INV-NOS-001 is the capstone book's license condition. If structural autonomy fails, then Books 1 through 7 are re-descriptions of node-property theory, not a distinct structural framework. The coherence of the entire AI Edition is contingent on this invariant holding.

invariants.label: Relational Primacy
invariants.statement: Relations are ontologically prior to the nodes they connect, not derivative from them. Nodes acquire their identity and structural role through the relations they stand in — not prior to, or independently of, those relations. There are no purely intrinsic structural relata: every node is constituted by its relational position.
invariants.formal: ∀n ∈ nodes(S): identity(n) = relational_profile(n, R_S)  where  relational_profile(n, R_S) = {r ∈ R_S : r.source = n ∨ r.target = n}
invariants.corollary: Two nodes with identical relational profiles within a structure are structurally identical, regardless of any difference in labeling or intrinsic designation. Structural identity is positional, not intrinsic. The 'same node in a different structure' is a category error — same-node identity requires same-relational-profile.
invariants.violation: Treating node identity as prior to relational assignment; asserting that a node retains its structural identity when removed from all relations; using node labels as proxies for structural identity without reference to relational profiles.
cross_references: INV-NOS-001 (Structural Autonomy — autonomy requires relational primacy as its mechanism)
INV-NOS-003 (Identity Through Change — relational profile is what is preserved across transformations)
INV-SARG-001 (Book 7 Argument Integrity — SARG node identity is relational, not positional-absolute)
invariants.tel_expression: INV[NOS-002]: assert (∀n ∈ nodes(S): identity(n) = {r ∈ R_S : (r.source = n) ∨ (r.target = n)})
invariants.meta_note: INV-NOS-002 is why SARG can detect argument structure purely from relation declarations (INV-SARG-001), why TEL composition is meaning-preserving (INV-TEL-003), and why OR opacity is a structural — not observer-relative — property (INV-OR-003). Each prior invariant is a domain expression of relational primacy.

invariants.label: Identity Through Change
invariants.statement: A structure retains its identity through a transformation if and only if the transformation preserves the structure's invariant set. Transformations that alter no invariant in the invariant set produce a structure that is numerically identical to the original. Transformations that alter at least one invariant produce a numerically distinct structure, regardless of how many nodes and relations remain unchanged.
invariants.formal: transform(S, T) preserves_identity(S) ⟺ invariant_set(transform(S, T)) = invariant_set(S)
invariants.corollary: Structural identity is not determined by element-retention (how many nodes or relations survive the transformation) but by invariant-set preservation. A transformation that removes 90% of nodes but preserves all invariants produces the same structure. A transformation that changes one node's relational profile in a way that violates one invariant produces a distinct structure, even if 99% of the configuration is unchanged.
invariants.violation: Measuring structural identity preservation by counting retained nodes or relations; declaring a transformation identity-preserving based on visual or topological similarity; treating invariant-set change as a quantitative degree rather than a binary identity boundary.
cross_references: INV-002 (Book 1 Constraint Preservation — INV-NOS-003 is the meta-theoretical generalization of INV-002)
INV-NOS-002 (Relational Primacy — what is preserved is the relational profile, not node count)
INV-TEL-004 (Book 5 Transformation Integrity — TEL transformations are valid iff they preserve constraint satisfaction; INV-NOS-003 is the ontological foundation of that rule)
invariants.meta_note: INV-NOS-003 answers the Ship of Theseus problem structurally: identity is preserved exactly when the invariant set is preserved. This is not a stipulation — it is the structural realist consequence of INV-NOS-001 and INV-NOS-002 applied to temporal or transformational contexts.

invariants.label: Abstraction Consistency
invariants.statement: Abstract structures and their instantiations share invariant structure. The invariant set of a valid instantiation is a superset of (or identical to) the invariant set of the abstract structure. Divergence between the invariant set of an abstract structure and that of a claimed instantiation indicates either (a) a modeling error — the claimed instantiation is not a genuine instance — or (b) genuine novelty — the instantiation carries structural properties absent from the abstract form, which then requires the abstract structure to be revised.
invariants.corollary: An instantiation that violates an invariant of its abstract structure is not an instance — it is either a distinct structure or a modeling error. Genuine novelty is the case where S_instance satisfies all invariants of S_abstract but also satisfies additional invariants not present in S_abstract — in this case, S_abstract should be revised upward, not treated as refuted.
invariants.violation: Accepting a claimed instantiation that violates an invariant of the abstract structure without classifying it as error or novelty; treating divergence as a matter of degree rather than a binary classification (error or novelty); revising the instantiation to suppress its novel invariants rather than propagating them to the abstract.
cross_references: INV-NOS-003 (Identity Through Change — abstraction is a class of transformations; INV-NOS-004 constrains which transformations are valid instantiations)
INV-NOS-001 (Structural Autonomy — abstract structures are defined by their relational configurations, not their instantiated elements)
INV-TEL-001 (Book 5 Expression Completeness — TEL must be complete over abstract structures; INV-NOS-004 demands the same of any representation language)
invariants.tel_expression: INV[NOS-004]: assert (∀S_a, S_i: instance(S_i, S_a) → invariant_set(S_a) ⊆ invariant_set(S_i))
invariants.meta_note: INV-NOS-004 is the AI Edition's self-application condition. The AI Edition itself is an abstract structure. Each book is a declared instantiation. If a book's formal content violates an invariant declared in the series manifest (AI_Edition_module.json), that book is either a modeling error or a source of genuine novelty requiring upward revision of the series abstract. This invariant closes the self-referential loop of Book 8.
